first_impression.reaction: Typed 'mykonos wedding venues' on the train. The first sentence tells me the five parts of the island where the venues are, so I've got my bearings before I scroll. The takeaways give me the guest range (25 to 800) and a summer heat warning, and there's a jump list. I'd read the takeaways, look at the table, tap the south coast because that's the Mykonos beaches I've heard of, check the FAQ, then bookmark.

journey.quote: Mykonos wedding venues fall into five parts of the island: the west-coast bays of Agios Ioannis and Ornos, closest to Mykonos Town; the south-coast beaches at Psarou and Platis Gialos; Elia further east; the quieter north coast at Agios Sostis; and a hilltop above Paradise beach.
journey.reaction: Answer in the first line, matches what I searched. Long sentence for a phone, but it does the job.

journey.quote: Guest count narrows the list quickly, because published capacity runs from 25 guests inside the Mykonos Grand chapel to weddings of up to 800 at Saint John.
journey.reaction: Real names, smallest to biggest in one line. This is the screenshot.

journey.quote: Four of these ten venues sit on the west coast at Agios Ioannis and Ornos, closest to Mykonos Town, while the rest spread along the south coast, Elia, the north coast and a hilltop above Paradise beach.
journey.reaction: I literally just read this in the intro. First takeaway is a repeat, so it feels like a wasted bullet.

journey.quote: Several venues have a chapel of their own, but the rules differ, from religious, civil and symbolic weddings at Grecotel Mykonos Lolita to religious weddings at Mykonos Grand only when both partners are Christian Orthodox.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that Orthodox thing. Useful, saves someone a nasty surprise.

journey.section: Mykonos wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Area | Type | Ceremony options | Largest published capacity | Exclusive use |
journey.reaction: Fewer columns than some tables, but still a sideways swipe on my phone to reach capacity. And the whole Exclusive use column is basically 'Not published' except one row.

journey.section: How to compare Mykonos venues like for like
journey.quote: Katikies Mykonos welcomes children above 13, which matters if your guest list includes young families.
journey.reaction: That's a real detail. Rules out a place fast if my cousins bring kids.

journey.quote: Six venues on this list have a chapel in the wedding plan.
journey.reaction: Wait, I've now had the chapel list in the takeaways, in the compare section and now again here. It's the same six names each time.

journey.section: Choosing an area of the island
journey.quote: A simple rule: if guests want to be near town, start on the west coast. If you want the beach in every photograph, look south. If you want privacy and a chapel, look north.
journey.reaction: Love this. Three lines and I know where to look. Honestly this could be higher up.

journey.quote: Up to 60 guests on the Ocean Balcony, and the wedding table and party for up to 120 in the L'Archipel restaurant and pool area.
journey.reaction: Specific numbers for ceremony and party separately. That's what I'd actually need for 80-ish people.

journey.quote: Not published: ceremony types, exclusive use, curfew.
journey.reaction: Every venue ends with a list of what's missing, and most of it already appeared in the bullets above it as 'Not published'. Same gap said twice per venue.

journey.section: Royal Myconian and Myconian Imperial, Elia
journey.quote: The kitchens are certified halal and kosher, and a South Asian chef cooks traditional Indian cuisine.
journey.reaction: Oh, that's genuinely useful for a mixed family guest list. Would send this one to my mum.

journey.section: ZeNIT Events Center, above Paradise beach
journey.quote: The venue's own services include a physician and medical room during events, security with CCTV, and guest transfers that ZeNIT runs itself for up to 16 guests, with larger groups handled through its partners and transfers by sea also offered.
journey.reaction: Nobody tells you this stuff. Feels like someone actually read the venue pages properly.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller says heatwaves are frequent in Greece over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion and heat stroke, and that many major tourist sites have little shade.
journey.reaction: Dated to this month, so I know it's current.

journey.quote: A date outside the summer months sits outside the heatwave and wildfire season.
journey.reaction: Okay but which months, then? The heading is 'When to marry' and I came out without a month to aim for. And the wind bit just says ask the venue.

journey.quote: Ask directly, because few venues publish it.
journey.reaction: Straight answer, even if the answer is 'nobody says'. Fine.

journey.quote: Can Australians legally get married in Mykonos?
journey.reaction: Australia again. I'm in Singapore. The whole legal section is Australian paperwork, so it's not for me.

journey.section: Shortlist your Mykonos venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: So it's an Australian company. Not sure they'd take me.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a Mykonos venue cost? Even a ballpark. Not one number on the page.
Which months are actually best? The page says avoid summer heat and asks about wind, but never names a month to aim for.
When is the wind worst? It calls Mykonos 'the island of the winds' but doesn't say when.
How far is each venue from the airport? Most don't say.
Do you work with couples outside Australia, and how do non-Australians handle the legal side?

turn_offs_found.quote: Not published: ceremony types, exclusive use, curfew.
turn_offs_found.why: Every one of the ten venues closes on a 'Not published' line that mostly repeats the 'Not published' bullets just above it. Skimming on my phone, I keep landing on what's missing instead of what's good about the place.

turn_offs_found.quote: Six venues on this list have a chapel in the wedding plan.
turn_offs_found.why: The same six chapel venues are listed in the takeaways, in 'Chapel, terrace or beach ceremony', in this section and again in the FAQ. It's a lot of scrolling for the same names before I get to venue number one.

turn_offs_found.quote: | Venue | Area | Type | Ceremony options | Largest published capacity | Exclusive use |
turn_offs_found.why: Still too wide for a phone, so I swipe sideways to get to capacity, and the Exclusive use column is 'Not published' in nine of ten rows, so that swipe gives me almost nothing.

turn_offs_found.quote: A date outside the summer months sits outside the heatwave and wildfire season.
turn_offs_found.why: The heading promises 'When to marry in Mykonos' but the section never names a month or season to pick. I wanted a quick answer and got 'not summer'.

turn_offs_found.quote: Four of these ten venues sit on the west coast at Agios Ioannis and Ornos, closest to Mykonos Town, while the rest spread along the south coast, Elia, the north coast and a hilltop above Paradise beach.
turn_offs_found.why: The first takeaway repeats the intro I just read. Takeaways are the one bit I definitely read, so a repeat there is a wasted slot.

would_share_with: A friend planning a Greek island wedding; I'd send her the takeaways and the 'simple rule' paragraph
My mum, for the halal, kosher and Indian kitchen line at the Elia hotels

cta_reaction.why: I'm just looking, not planning yet. The links are inline, no pop-ups, and they only show up a few times, so they didn't annoy me. I'd bookmark before I'd enquire, and the 'AUD for Australian couples' line makes me think it isn't for me anyway.

top_3_changes: Cut the repeated chapel lists: keep the full list once (the 'Where the chapels are' section) and trim the mentions in the compare section and FAQ to a pointer, and swap the first takeaway for something new, such as the 'simple rule' about which coast to pick.

Drop the closing 'Not published:' line from each venue (the bullets already say it), and either drop the Exclusive use column from the at-a-glance table or replace it with something most rows can fill, so it reads on a phone.
Make 'When to marry in Mykonos' answer its own heading: name the months that sit outside the heatwave and wildfire season, and say when the wind is usually strongest, if a source supports it.

assumptions: Persona is provisional (weight 0.10); reactions reflect generic informational search intent.

Arrived from a Google search for 'mykonos wedding venues' on a phone; read the intro and takeaways, glanced at the table, scrolled through the compare, chapel and area sections, jumped to the south coast and Elia, peeked at ZeNIT, then the weather section, FAQ and closing.
Prices are deliberately not printed; the missing ballpark is logged as an unanswered question only.

The Australia-focused framing (AUD, legal section, FAQ) is logged as a low-severity objection and unanswered question from a non-Australian reader, not a must-fix, since the business focus is deferred.
The month-to-aim-for change is conditional on a source; no climate facts were invented.
Read with images not yet loaded; image slots and HTML comments judged as invisible.
Quotes with inline HTML fact comments, link markup or bold markers are given as a reader sees them.
